---
title: "How do I convert observations into percentages by category?"
---

## The question

How do I convert observations into percentages by category?

## What to check and do

1. Identify the category of each observation. 2. Count the categories and divide each count by the total. 3. Check missing values and rounding.

## Worked example: mtcars

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
answer <- ru_apply("relative_frequency", data=d, x="cyl")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(answer$proportion),1)))
```

The output reports what proportion of the cars in this dataset have each cylinder count. It does not describe all cars on the road.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("relative_frequency", data=your_data, x="category_column")
```

When a table already contains frequencies, weight its counts rather than counting each row once.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("relative_frequency")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
